entityTypes.description: A business owner or operator who has registered a store on the LetBuyy platform. Identified by site_id. Owns one or more stores and manages products, orders, payments, and settings.

A tenant-scoped commerce store on the LetBuyy platform. Identified by site_id and store slug. Hosts products, collections, customers, orders, and a theme. Accessible at {slug}.letbuyy.com or a custom domain.
A visual and layout presentation layer for a storefront. Can be a Liquid template or a React component tree. Managed by theme-engine. Each store uses exactly one active theme.
A third-party or first-party application installed on a store via the app marketplace. Extends store functionality through APIs and webhooks.
A customer purchase record within a store. Contains order_items, shipping details, GST invoice data, payment status, and fulfilment state. Money stored as *_minor bigint (paise).
A financial transaction record associated with an order. Processed via Razorpay or COD. Stored in payment_transactions. Mutations only via SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.
A shopper registered with a store. Identified by store_customers row. Holds customer_credentials for authentication. Scoped to a single store's site_id.
An operational event indicating degradation, failure, or anomaly in a service or domain. Triggers runbook execution, escalation, and blast-radius analysis.
A code or configuration change released to a production environment. Can cause incidents if it breaks dependent services. Tracked by commit SHA and Vercel/Cloudflare deploy ID.
A runtime process in the LetBuyy topology: api-gateway, customer-web, merchant-web, identity-platform, queue-workers, webhook-service, or mobile-bff.
An async work queue processed by queue-workers. Carries tenant-scoped jobs (emails, webhooks, inventory updates). Jobs are HMAC-signed envelopes.
A Cloudflare Worker or Node.js process consuming queue jobs or serving edge requests. Part of the queue-workers or api-gateway runtime.
A business capability subdomain in the LetBuyy platform (e.g. payments, orders, themes, identity, marketplace). Groups related tables, RPCs, routes, queues, and workers.
An architecture, design, audit, or operational document in docs/. Captures decisions, findings, runbooks, and domain knowledge.
A database schema migration applied to the Supabase/Postgres instance. Alters tables, policies, triggers, or functions. Immutable once applied to production.

relationships.description: A merchant owns and operates one or more stores.
A store uses exactly one active theme for its storefront presentation.
A store installs marketplace apps to extend its functionality.
A customer places one or more orders within a store.
An order is settled through one or more payment transactions.
An incident degrades or blocks one or more merchants and their stores.
A deployment can introduce regressions that cause operational incidents.
A deployment updates the code or configuration of one or more services.
A service (worker) processes jobs from an async queue.
A service is the primary owner of a business domain area.
A document captures knowledge, decisions, or runbooks for a domain area.
A database migration alters the schema of tables owned by a domain area.
One domain area has a runtime or data dependency on another domain area.
